front.title: Interoperability, Security Evaluation, and Negative Testing for Attested TLS 1.3 and DTLS 1.3

abstract.t:
This document defines a framework for reproducible interoperability and security evaluation of implementations that integrate remote attestation with TLS 1.3 and DTLS 1.3. It complements protocol and architecture specifications by defining test profiles, a common result model, cross-implementation procedures, negative tests, and measurements at the boundary between transport authentication, attestation appraisal, authorization, and application-data release.
In addition to per-connection attestation, the framework evaluates reusable Attestation Results and cross-connection trust-continuity mechanisms, including deployments in which an attestation endpoint and application-serving endpoint are distinct. It addresses key custody and derivation, target and workload identity, state drift, credential lifecycle, multi-relying-party isolation, proxy topology, session resumption, early data, privacy, and failure containment.
This document does not define a new attestation architecture, Evidence format, TLS or DTLS extension, cryptographic key schedule, or remote-attestation protocol. It specifies an evaluation framework for comparing implementations and identifying interoperability and security gaps in declared profiles.
